Piedmont Park Promenade and Magnolia Hal.description: The Promenade and Magnolia Hall form a landscaped event and arrival zone near the park's northern side; private events can change access around the building and terrace.

Oak Hill and Meadow.description: Oak Hill and the adjoining meadow provide broad skyline views, picnic space, and room for festivals; the lawn is exposed and event setup can temporarily limit access.

Gateway of Dreams sculpture.description: Gateway of Dreams is the 55-foot Baron Pierre de Coubertin sculpture and a free outdoor photo landmark near the park's northern downtown edge.

Androgyne Planet sculpture.description: Androgyne Planet is a prominent Olympic-era sculpture along the park paths; it is an outdoor art stop rather than a playground or climbing feature.

Centennial Olympic Park water gardens.description: The water gardens are ornamental pools and landscaped paths that offer a quieter park stop; they are not a splash pad or permitted wading area.

North Avenue entrance and promenade.description: The North Avenue side is a practical arrival from Ponce City Market and the BeltLine, with a paved promenade and busy street crossings nearby.

Ralph McGill Boulevard entrance.description: The Ralph McGill Boulevard entrance reaches the lower basin and southern paths; expect grades between this arrival, the playground, and upper park facilities.

Grant Park Gateway and parking deck.description: The Gateway combines the major Boulevard arrival, paid parking deck, restrooms, and access toward Zoo Atlanta and the park's family amenities.

Grant Park Farmers Market area.description: The farmers market uses a scheduled park area for vendors and community gatherings; market dates and large events can change parking and circulation.

Westside Park main gateway.description: The monumental main gateway is the clearest first-time arrival and orientation point, but the reservoir overlook and playground still require a substantial walk.

Upper meadow and picnic lawn.description: The upper meadow offers open picnic and play space above the reservoir landscape; it has limited shade and does not provide access to the protected water.

Chastain Arts Center.description: Chastain Arts Center is a staffed city facility for classes, studios, and exhibitions, with building hours and program access separate from general park hours.

Chastain Horse Park.description: Chastain Horse Park is an operating equestrian facility with lessons and events; visitors should use its designated access and confirm public program times.

John Lewis Freedom Parkway plaza.description: The John Lewis Freedom Parkway plaza is a civic landmark and public-art stop along the park corridor, reached by paved paths near busy city streets.

Candler Park trail connection.description: The Candler Park connection extends the trail network east through neighborhood streets and green space; cyclists and families should plan for street crossings.

BeltLine Kroger and 725 Ponce access.description: This busy BeltLine access provides nearby groceries, food, elevators, and private garage parking; garage prices and validation rules are not park-controlled.

Inman Park access at Elizabeth Street.description: The Elizabeth Street access is a useful neighborhood entry near food and transit, with heavy shared trail traffic and active street crossings at peak times.

Cascade Springs trailhead and parking.description: The main trailhead is the orientation point for the preserve's parking, map, and wooded routes; the small lot can fill and trails become muddy after rain.

Picnic area and stone shelter.description: The picnic area and stone shelter provide a rustic gathering stop near the trail network; the structure should not be treated as safe shelter during severe weather.

Perkerson Park basketball courts.description: The outdoor basketball courts support casual and programmed play; leagues, maintenance, or organized use may take priority at busy times.

Perkerson Park fitness zone.description: The outdoor fitness zone provides free exercise equipment near the park paths, with limited weather protection and surfaces that can become hot in summer.
